shelf.notes: Clean frame, planked back and cap read well, but two contract problems. Palette: the pale honey boards are a second wood tone outside the walnut family, and honey oak is reserved for doors/table tops/bench seats (§3). Dressing: shelves are empty — a tavern shelf should carry bottles, mugs, or plates per the tableware grammar. Three-quarter view also hints the boards stop short of the right stile;

round-table.notes: Palette conforms: honey-oak top, warm brown pedestal, no second wood tone; proportions and pedestal grammar match prompt. Main issue: tabletop rim silhouette is scalloped/lumpy instead of a smooth disc with soft bevel, so it reads bread-like at side view. Fix rim smoothness; then bake to confirm c9a06a rim wear.

stool.notes: Palette conforms: honey-oak seat, warm #8a5a35 legs, no walnut drift. Round seat, three splayed legs, low ring stretcher match the stool contract; grounded and centered. Chunky chibi forms read at 128 px. Minor: seat reads thin for the 'thick seat' spec, and the pale #c9a06a edge wear is barely visible in the render.

table.notes: Palette conforms: top and legs stay inside the honey-oak family, no off-palette wood tone. Bare top is correct for wave 1 since candles and mugs are separate assets. Leg/stretcher grammar is still unlocked per §5; consider plank seams on the top when furniture grammar lands.
